How to use this calculator

  1. Enter consumption, investment, government purchases and the remaining inputs.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How gdp is calculated

Estimate gross domestic product with the expenditure identity: household consumption plus investment plus government purchases plus exports minus imports. Enter values in one consistent currency and time period; this computes a nominal total and does not adjust for inflation or population. C=500, I=120, G=200, X=80, M=100 gives GDP of 800 in the chosen units. The calculation validates each input and keeps its stated units explicit. Imported goods may appear in consumption or investment but were not produced domestically. This is an estimate for the stated assumptions; confirm measurements and any applicable professional or local standards before relying on it.

GDP = consumption + investment + government + exports − imports
A worked example

C=500, I=120, G=200, X=80, M=100 gives GDP of 800 in the chosen units.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

Why are imports subtracted?

Imported goods may appear in consumption or investment but were not produced domestically.

Is this real GDP?

No. Real GDP requires price-index adjustment across periods.
